newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Tribal rebels and Bangladesh begin peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Tribal rebels and Bangladesh begin peace talks.

text.p: Tribal rebel leaders and the government on Sunday began peace talks aimed at ending decades-old insurgency in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, officials said.
They said the talks were being held in a cordial atmosphere and might continue on Monday to hammer out solutions to the crisis in the region.
A team of rebel Shanti Bahini (peace force) leaders, led by Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma, flew to the capital on Sunday for their third meeting with government leaders since January.

The Shanti Bahini has been fighting a bush war since 1973 in the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, over demands for political autonomy and expulsion of about 500,000 Bengali-speaking settlers from the area.
Over 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, according to official figures.
Officials in the Hill Tracts said the settlers on Sunday enforced a strike against what they said the government willingness to give concessions to the tribals at the talks.
"We want peace in the Hill Tracts, but not at the cost of our rights," Mohammad Shahajuddin, a leader of the Bengali settlers, told Reuters by telephone.
The officials said the strike was peaceful and there was no report of any violence.
